Wikipedia (fetched 2026-10-29): founded 1970 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, first as a store called Free People; renamed Urban Outfitters and incorporated in 1976. Founders Richard Hayne, Judy Wicks and Scott Belair. Headquarters Philadelphia. Owned by the public company Urban Outfitters, Inc. (Nasdaq: URBN), whose other brands include Anthropologie, Free People, Terrain, BHLDN and the Vetri Family restaurant group.

Wikipedia: the Urban Outfitters store sells women's and men's apparel, footwear, beauty and wellness, accessories, activewear, housewares and music (mainly vinyl records and cassettes); much of the merchandise is designed and produced by the company's wholesale division under multiple private labels (not named on the page).

Status set to verified from the parent company's official annual report (enrich.md §2 parent-company rule): URBN Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/912615/000119312526137916/urbn-20260131.htm) says 'Urban Outfitters targets young adults aged 18 to 28' and carries 'women's and men's fashion apparel, activewear, intimates, footwear, accessories, home goods, electronics and beauty'; 'A large portion of our merchandise is exclusive to Urban Outfitters', designed internally or with third-party brands; BDG and iets frans are its apparel collections (also sold wholesale). Stores at January 31, 2026: 253 Urban Outfitters stores, 177 in North America and 76 in Europe, plus franchisee stores in the Middle East; websites and apps in North America and Europe. The filing doesn't split US from Canada, so us_stores stays empty. known_for paraphrases the 10-K target-customer line plus its merchandise list; a human should confirm against the store's own tagline. Prices, sizes, shipping and returns still need a human read of the store.
